summary:
ARES-X is an interactive, bilingual web platform that catalogs and maps terrestrial analogs to Mars, environments on Earth that replicate the geological, mineralogical, and extreme climatic conditions of the Red Planet.

The platform features a curated database of 32 global and local analog sites, highlighting strategic volcanic and extreme ecosystems in Costa Rica alongside international landmarks, supported by geographic filtering and an interactive crowdsourcing module that enables researchers, students, and citizens to register new Mars alike locations.

By democratizing access to planetary analog data and encouraging collaborative mapping, ARES-X bridges the gap between Earth science and space exploration. Studying these accessible terrestrial environments is vital for testing aerospace instrumentation, training mission crews, and validating astrobiological models, proving that understanding Mars begins with exploring and preserving extreme environments right here on Earth.
details:
What It Does & How It Works ARES-X is an interactive, bilingual (English/Spanish) web application designed to explore, filter, and crowdsource terrestrial analogs to Mars. Users can browse a curated catalog of 32 Mars-like environments on Earth, filter locations geographically (distinguishing strategic sites in Costa Rica from global landmarks), and inspect the geological and climatic parallels of each site. Additionally, the platform features an interactive submission module that allows users to propose and register new terrestrial locations capable of simulating Martian conditions.

Benefits & Intended Impact Studying Mars directly is costly and logistically complex, whereas terrestrial analogs offer accessible, real-world laboratories. ARES-X democratizes planetary science by making comparative planetology intuitive for students, educators, and researchers. Its intended impact is twofold: fostering STEM engagement by showing that space exploration starts in our own backyard, and building a collaborative repository that highlights local extreme ecosystems—such as Costa Rica’s volcanic terrains—as valuable assets for astrobiological research, rover testing, and mission simulation.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Frontend & Core Technologies: Built with HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript for fast, lightweight performance across desktop and mobile browsers without heavy dependencies.
  • Architecture & Deployment: Hosted and deployed via GitHub Pages (github.io), using dynamic DOM manipulation for real-time language switching, category filtering, and interactive user submissions.

Creativity & Key Considerations Rather than presenting static scientific tables, ARES-X frames planetary geology as an interactive exploration journey, bridging global space science with local biodiversity and geography. When designing the solution, our team prioritized accessibility (full bilingual support in Spanish and English), low-bandwidth performance (clean, responsive web architecture usable in classrooms or field locations), scalability (community-driven data expansion), and regional relevance by spotlighting under-represented volcanic analogs in Latin America alongside well-known international sites.
